names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 14 aprilie, «Sfântul Ierarh Martin Mărturisitorul, Episcopul Romei»; the bare personal name, without the rank the line carries.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's first heading for the Julian 14 April on pravoslavno.rs, „Св. Мартин исповедник, папа Римски.“, with Св. left off — it is not a rank — and with исповедник and папа Римски left off as well: the first is the rank word this folder already carries in `types`, and the second is the see, which this corpus keeps in `office` and which this folder already has there. The heading leaves no epithet, so the bare forename is what the source gives.

Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 14 апреля ст. ст., name page 1488, «Святитель Мартин I Римский, папа, исповедник», with the rank words and the office left off; the day's own line gives the name in the genitive and the see as «папы Римского», which is this folder's `office`. The regnal number is part of the name the calendar's link gives and is kept. `.tmp/foldchk.py` reports no folder holding this form.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 14 апреля ст. ст. — «Свт. Мартина исп., папы Римского (655).»
source.note: The day's first entry and the only one of the six to carry a typikon icon, whose alt reads «Cовершается служба, не отмеченная в Типиконе никаким знаком» — a service the Typikon marks with no sign at all. **It keeps him on the Romanian and Serbian calendars' day and not the Greek one**, which this folder's own rows put on 20 September and on a second Greek page on 13 April; one row per church, so nothing was moved. Its year, 655, is the year this folder already carries, and its life closes «+ 16 сентября 655» — the 16 September, which is what the Greek 20 September day is about and which no source read for this folder had stated before. The name page (1488) gives «День памяти: 14 апреля» and no other day. The day prints one hymn under his name, a troparion in the fourth tone, added here with its English.

feast.note: The Romanian calendar keeps him on 14 April; the Greek synaxarion this folder already cited keeps him on 13 April.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 14 aprilie — «Sfântul Ierarh Martin Mărturisitorul, Episcopul Romei»
Ορθόδοξος Συναξαριστής (saint.gr), 20 Σεπτεμβρίου — «Άγιοι Μαρτίνος Πάπας Ρώμης και Μάξιμος ο ομολογητής ο σοφώτατος»
Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 27.04.2026 (14. април ст. ст.) — „Св. Мартин исповедник, папа Римски.“

attestations.note: The day's first of three entries, and **on the Romanian calendar's day and not the Greek one**: doxologia keeps him on 14 April and saint.gr on 20 September, and the Prologue's menologion 14 April is the Romanian's number; one row per church, so the Greek row kept its day and nothing moved. The man is the same beyond doubt, and the **655 agrees exactly** with what this folder holds, so **no date was touched**. The entry is long and almost all of it is new to the folder: that he **became pope on 5 July 649**, in the thick of the quarrel with the Monothelites; that the emperor was **Constans II, Heraclius's grandson**, and the patriarch of Constantinople Paul; that the emperor wrote the **Typos** himself to make peace and it pleased the heretics; that Martin called **a council of 105 bishops** which condemned it; that he wrote to the patriarch asking him to hold the pure Orthodox faith and to counsel the emperor off the heretical subtleties, and that the letter angered patriarch and emperor both; that the commander **Olympius** was sent to bring the pope bound and **did not dare to bind him, but suborned a soldier to kill him in church with a hidden sword — and the soldier went blind the moment he came in**; that Olympius then went to Sicily against the Saracens and died there; that a second commander was sent on the charge that the pope **colluded with the Saracens and did not honour the most pure Mother of God**, and the pope's answer, that the first was slander and that **«as for the most pure Mother of God, if anyone does not honour and confess her and does not bow to her, let him be accursed in this age and in the age to come»**; the long sickness in prison at Constantinople, in narrowness and hunger; the sentence of exile to **Cherson**, where he lived two years; and that **the patriarch died two years before him and, visited by the emperor on his deathbed, turned his head to the wall and wept, confessing that he had sinned much against Martin and begging the emperor to set him free**. **Three names are given in the entry's own Serbian forms in the life rather than in English, and the reason is a measurement**: a bare English «Paul» is the exact display name of two folders, `paul-the-apostle` and `paul-bishop-of-nicaea`, neither of whom is this Monothelite patriarch, and `tests/related-floor.test.mjs` reads the names a life prints in prose, so the English form would have asked for a `related` row false in both directions. The same holds for the second commander, whose bare English form is two other folders' display name. The entry's own forms stand instead and the men are identified with nobody. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: Died 16 September 655 at Cherson, saint.gr (13 April).

hymns.text: Îndreptător credinţei şi chip blândeţelor, învăţător înfrânării te-a arătat pe tine, turmei tale, adevărul lucrurilor. Pentru aceasta ai dobândit cu smerenia cele înalte şi cu sărăcia cele bogate; Părinte Ierarhe Martin, roagă pe Hristos Dumnezeu să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Ierarh Martin Mărturisitorul, Episcopul Romei», Glasul 4

english.text: A rule of faith and an image of gentleness, a teacher of abstinence: so the truth of things has shown you to your flock. Therefore you gained by humility the things on high, and by poverty the things that are rich. Father and hierarch Martin, entreat Christ God to save our souls.

hymns.text: Θείοις δόγμασι, τῆς εὐσέβειας, ὑπεστήριξας, τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν, ὦ Μαρτίνε ἱεράρχα Θεόσοφε, τὸν γὰρ Χριστὸν διπλοῦν ὄντα ταὶς φύσεσιν, ὁμολογήσας τὴν πλάνην κατήσχυνας. Πάτερ Ὅσιε Χριστὸν τὸν Θεὸν ἱκέτευε, δωρήσασθαι ἠμὶν τὸ μέγα ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr — Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος γ', Θείας πίστεως, on the page of Άγιος Μαρτίνος πάπας Ρώμης και δύο Επισκόπων, saint.gr's 13 Απριλίου. It is his own and names him.

english.text: With the divine teachings of piety thou didst uphold the Church, O Martin, hierarch wise in God; for confessing Christ to be twofold in his natures thou didst put the error to shame. Venerable father, entreat Christ God that great mercy be given to us.

hymns.text: Ὡς Ἱεράρχης τῶν ἀῤῥήτων και διδάσκαλος, Θεολογίας ἀληθοῦς ἐκφάντωρ πέφηνας, καὶ ἀνέβλυσας Μαρτῖνε δογμάτων ρεῖθρα· Τὸν Χριστὸν γὰρ ἐν δυσί τελείαις φύσεσι, καὶ θελήσεσι πανσόφως ἐδογμάτισας, τοῖς βοῶσί σοι, χαίροις Πάτερ πανόλβιε.

source.text: saint.gr — Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’, Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ, on the page of Άγιος Μαρτίνος πάπας Ρώμης και δύο Επισκόπων, saint.gr's 13 Απριλίου. It is his own, names him, and states the two wills the Monothelites denied.

english.text: As a hierarch and teacher of things unspeakable thou wast shown a declarer of the true theology, and didst pour out streams of doctrine, O Martin; for in all wisdom thou didst teach Christ in two perfect natures and two wills, to those who cry to thee: rejoice, all-blessed father.

hymns.text: Истинных повелений устне распространил еси, / зловерие низложил еси, Богомудре Мартине, / святителю всечестне, / поминай нас, угодниче Христов, / еже к Нему ходатайствы твоими, / да в мире устроиши живот наш.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 14 апреля ст. ст. — «Тропарь святого Мартина Исповедника, папы Римского», глас 4, under «Молитвы»
source.note: One of the four hymns the day prints; the other three are the Vilnius company's. It names this saint and no other. Copied out of the page by `.tmp/rubody.mjs` rather than retyped.

english.text: You spread abroad the lips of true commandments and cast down false belief, O God-wise Martin, all-honourable hierarch. Remember us, O servant of Christ, by your intercessions to him, that you may order our life in peace.
